questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It's not a nice room. It's very hot. It is not allowed to have air condition, but you can smuggle one in if you want to risk it. The fan is super loud, and does not cool the room sufficiently.

But the daily life is vibrant and there is lots of people, both locals, exchangers and people from all around the world coming to study at NUS. Lots of activities in the dorms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: goes from 5 to 4 because of the room and the fact that I didn't have air condition

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Tedious but easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to complete a course on academic integrity and sexual consent as part of registration. Then set up your student mail. Go to a physical place on campus to pick up student card. Had to show proof of vaccinations, which I couldn't because Denmark stopped using the digitally verifiable vaccine pass. So I had to get a serology test in the campus health center, to verify that I had vaccine antibodies. This was tedious but not hard.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: NUS Support mail and asking around
